The iconic 11-cm bronze statuette known as the Dancing Girl from Mohenjo-Daro has been reinstalled at the National Museum in New Delhi, putting to rest the recent controversy over its removal. But questions remain about the protection, permanent display and changing interpretations of this 4,500-year-old artefact.
Why has this bronze figurine remained at the centre of cultural and historical debate? ThePrint Columnist Disha Ahluwalia explains in this week’s column
